newsitem.title: USA: Dow see-saws to first record close of new year.
newsitem.headline: Dow see-saws to first record close of new year.

text.p: Wall Street stocks turned in a tumultuous session on Monday, with the Dow industrials and Nasdaq each clawing their way to record highs.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 23 points to close unofficially at 6567. The closing mark was the Dow's first all-time high of the year and erased its previous record of 6560.91, which was set on December 27 and represented the Dow's 44th record close of 1996.
The Nasdaq Composite also tagged its first record high of 1997, rising 5.74 points to end unofficially at 1316.42.
The new high was Nasdaq's first since December 9.

Despite the records, the overall performance was mixed, with broad indicators showing little of the momentum manifested by blue chips. And even the Dow ended well off its peaks, pulled down sharply by a series of late sell programs.
What strength stocks did show was concentrated among cyclicals, which benefited from a growing perception that the economy continues to expand at a solid pace.
"There's no question that the recent numbers have continued to run on the strong side," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
"Housing, construction and consumer confidence have all been strong," Canelo said. "The first implication of all that is just better earnings."
The earnings argument, which propelled the Dow to a 101.60 gain last Friday, held sway for most of the session and paced the Dow to a better than 60 point rally.
But even as stocks were rising, trepidation that economic growth could also spell higher inflation ate away at the bond market, where interest rates crept steadily higher all day.
Eventually, analysts said, that concern spread to the stock market.

"If rates are trending higher, you don't buy bank stocks and bank stocks were weak today," noted Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "That shows the thought of higher rates was creeping into investment decisions."
According to Birinyi Associates, a pair of afternoon program trades slashed about 71 points off the Dow industrials and the programs also pulled the S&P 500 index to a fractional loss for the day.
Market breadth was moderately positive, with advancing issues outnumbering decliners by about five to four.
Volume was heavy, totalling more than 530 million shares on the NYSE in what was essentially the first fully-staffed session of the new year.

Cyclical stocks held firmest to their gains. Among the strongest was General Motors Corp, which added 1-3/8 to 59-1/4. Smith Barney upgraded the shares to buy from outperform and raised its 1997 earnings estimate on GM to $8.00 per share from $7.80.
Oil shares were also strong, as cold weather across the U.S. drove domestic crude prices above $26 per barrel.
Texaco Inc rose 1-3/8 to 102 and Exxon Corp gained 1-3/8 to 100.
Toys R Us tumbled 4-5/8 to 26-1/8 after the company said it had registered disappointing Christmas season sales.
Apple Computer Corp skidded 3-7/8 to 17-7/8 in the first trading since it announced late Friday that its fiscal first quarter loss would far exceed Wall Street expectations.
Several Wall Street downgraded the shares, and expressed doubts about Apple's ability to revive its business soon.

Bank stocks were generally lower, pressured by the weaker bond market and rising interest rates. Chase Manhattan Corp fell 7/8 to 87-3/8, Citicorp fell 3/4 to 103-3/4 and First Union Corp eased 5/8 to 74.
The S&P 500 fell 0.38 to 747.65.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 5.72 to a record 1316.40.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
